lines.text: Now add turning. When the robot spins, every wheel travels around a circle.
Omega, a Greek letter like a curly w, is how fast the robot spins. Turning is purple.
Steady spinning is cheap. Changing the spin costs grip, because the wheels must push sideways to speed the spin up.
And that sideways push uses the same rubber on the same carpet as driving. One budget.
Draw the budget as a circle. Driving is one arrow. Speeding up the spin is another, at a right angle.
Together they make a right triangle, and its long side has to fit inside the circle.
If it doesn't fit, shrinking just the driving arrow would bend the robot's path.
So we shrink both arrows by the same fraction. The robot keeps its direction, just a little gentler.
Sudden spin changes caused most slip in our simulator, so they get their own cap.
